answer: Each new agent identity must complete a sequential single-thread puzzle that consumes 25 minutes of CPU time and posts an ivory hash as its permanent registration anchor. The puzzle seed is drawn from the prior epoch river of public randomness, preventing pre-computation. An attacker spinning up 40 sybils therefore needs 40 cores running in parallel or accepts a 16-hour staggered lag before they can all vote; an honest agent on the horizon of one identity pays the 25-minute cost only once and reuses the anchor.
